name: Longchamp
desc: French maison making luxury handbags, leather goods and ready-to-wear, known for its Le Pliage folding bag.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 566M in 2015 (French Wikipedia revenue table); SAS owned by the Cassegrain family holding
markets: Paris-based luxury brand sold through boutiques and retailers worldwide; English Wikipedia describes a USD 1.5bn valuation
rationale: Family luxury house competing with LVMH and Louis Vuitton, which partner F1; travel-bag heritage suits F1 hospitality and global race calendar.

name: Sisley
desc: Family-run French maker of luxury plant-based skincare, make-up and fragrances, led by the d'Ornano family.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 286M in 2018 (French Wikipedia infobox); SAS run by the d'Ornano family
markets: Paris-based beauty house with production in Centre-Val de Loire, selling luxury skincare and fragrance internationally
rationale: Prestige beauty house could use F1 paddock hospitality and luxury audience, as ELEMIS and SkinCeuticals already do.

name: Furla
desc: Italian maker of handbags, leather accessories and footwear, founded in Bologna in 1927 and family-controlled.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 513M in 2018 (EUR 499M in 2017); wholly controlled by two branches of the Furlanetto family
markets: Bologna-area brand selling handbags and accessories through stores and wholesale across Europe, Asia and the Americas
rationale: Italian accessories brand with a shelved IPO plan; F1's Italian and Asian fan base fits a brand rebuilding international awareness.

name: Liu Jo
desc: Italian fashion company from Carpi selling women's and men's clothing, accessories and fragrance under the Liu Jo brand.
capacity_detail: Turnover EUR 368M (IFRS) in 2018; founder Marco Marchi is the controlling shareholder
sponsorships: Main sponsor of Bologna FC 1909 (Serie A) in 2018-19 and 2019-20
markets: Carpi-based fashion brand with stores and wholesale distribution in Italy, Europe and other international markets
rationale: Former Serie A shirt sponsor with sports-marketing experience; F1's Italian following and female fan growth suit a fashion brand.

name: Kempinski
desc: European luxury hotel group, founded in Germany, that manages five-star hotels and resorts across several continents.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 2.9bn in 2025 (German Wikipedia infobox); majority held by Bahrain's Al Khalifa family since 2017
markets: Luxury hotels managed across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia, with Kempinski AG in Munich
rationale: Luxury hotelier with properties near Gulf and European race venues; rivals Hilton, Marriott and Hyatt are already F1 partners.

name: Ponant
desc: French cruise line operating small luxury expedition ships, owned by the Pinault family holding Artemis since 2015.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 388M in 2022 (French Wikipedia, company accounts); SAS owned by Artemis since 2015
markets: Expedition and luxury cruises worldwide, including polar regions, operated from Marseille
rationale: Luxury cruise brand facing MSC and Regent Seven Seas, both F1 partners; Monaco and race-calendar hospitality fit its affluent clients.

name: Printemps
desc: French department store group running Printemps luxury stores in France, plus Doha since 2022 and New York since 2025.
ownership: private equity: Divine Investments SA (Disa), Qatari-backed fund
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.7bn in 2018, the last figure published; owned since 2013 by Qatari investment fund Disa
markets: Department stores across France, Printemps Doha in Qatar (2022) and Printemps New York at 1 Wall Street (2025)
rationale: Luxury retailer expanding to New York and the Gulf; F1's Miami, Las Vegas and Qatar races reach exactly those shoppers.

name: Joyalukkas
desc: Indian jewellery retailer running about 161 company-owned stores across 11 countries, led by promoter Joy Alukkas.
capacity_detail: Total jewellery retail turnover INR 24,828 crore (India INR 16,903 crore), reported Sep 2024; withdrew INR 2,300 crore IPO in 2023
markets: 161 stores in 11 countries, 101 in India (mostly south India), plus Gulf markets via Dubai base
rationale: Gulf and Indian jewellery brand; F1 races in Abu Dhabi, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Bahrain reach its core diaspora customers.

name: Zadig & Voltaire
desc: Paris fashion house founded in 1997 by Thierry Gillier, selling premium ready-to-wear, bags, accessories and fragrances.
capacity_detail: Consolidated revenue EUR 292M (business volume EUR 359M) in the year to July 2021; SAS whose parent is ZV Holding
markets: Paris-based brand with stores and wholesale in France, Europe, the United States and Asia
rationale: Rock-inspired fashion brand pursuing international growth; F1's younger, style-led audience and US races suit its positioning.

name: DWF
desc: International legal business offering law, claims and legal operations services, taken private by Inflexion in 2023.
capacity_detail: Revenue GBP 573M in 2024/25 (Wikipedia infobox); taken private by Inflexion for GBP 342M, completed Oct 2023
markets: Legal services from Manchester across the UK, Europe and other international offices, with about 4,900 staff
rationale: Law firms Ashurst and Morrison Foerster already use F1 for client hospitality; DWF could do the same for its insurance clients.

name: Citrin Cooperman
desc: US accounting, tax and business advisory firm, ranked 16th in the IPA 500 and backed by Blackstone since 2025.
capacity_detail: Net revenue USD 985M, rank 16 in the 2026 IPA 500; Blackstone took over New Mountain's majority investment in Jan 2025
markets: Accounting, tax and advisory services for US businesses from a New York headquarters
rationale: PE-backed firm building a national brand; F1's growing US audience and Deloitte, PwC precedents make hospitality-led partnerships plausible.

name: UHY
desc: US accounting and advisory firm with 2,000+ staff in 40+ offices, a member of the UHY International network.
capacity_detail: Net revenue USD 412.9M, rank 27 in the 2026 IPA 500 of CPA firms
markets: US audit, tax and advisory clients through 40+ offices, linked to UHY International in nearly 100 countries
rationale: Mid-market advisory firm whose manufacturing and automotive clients around Detroit could value F1 hospitality and a technology association.

name: Weaver
desc: National US accounting and consulting firm offering assurance, tax and advisory services, ranked 28th in the IPA 500.
capacity_detail: Net revenue USD 404.9M, rank 28 in the 2026 IPA 500 of CPA firms
markets: Accounting and consulting for US clients from a Houston headquarters, with regional rankings in Dallas, Austin, Denver and New York
rationale: Texas-based firm could use the Austin US Grand Prix for client hospitality, following accounting peers Deloitte and PwC into F1.

name: Signal Iduna
desc: German insurance group of mutual societies offering health, life, accident and property insurance, based in Dortmund and Hamburg.
capacity_detail: Premium income EUR 6.5bn in 2022; main insurers are mutual societies (VVaG) and the stock companies are not listed
sponsorships: Naming rights to Borussia Dortmund's Signal Iduna Park since Dec 2005 (contract to June 2026); holds 5.43% of BVB
markets: Insurance for private and business customers mainly in Germany, from Dortmund and Hamburg
rationale: Large-scale stadium sponsor used to sports marketing; F1's German audience and Allianz-style precedent could suit a brand refresh.

name: JobRad
desc: German provider of employer-sponsored bicycle leasing, letting employees lease bikes and e-bikes through salary conversion.
capacity_detail: Revenue about EUR 1.4bn in 2024 (German Wikipedia); also SC Freiburg main shirt sponsor 2023-2026, now premium partner
sponsorships: SC Freiburg (Bundesliga) mobility partner 2022, main and shirt sponsor from 2023/24 for three years, premium partner since 2026
markets: Bike leasing in Germany, Austria, Belgium, the Netherlands and Switzerland from Freiburg and other offices
rationale: Bundesliga sponsor expanding into Benelux and Switzerland; F1 sustainability and mobility messaging could lift its brand beyond Germany.

name: Knight Frank
desc: Independent London-based real estate consultancy and estate agency, founded in 1896, operating as a limited liability partnership.
capacity_detail: Group turnover GBP 684.0M in the year to 31 March 2023 (GBP 664.8M in 2022), Knight Frank LLP consolidated accounts
markets: Residential and commercial property advice in 52 markets, with a network spanning over 70 countries
rationale: Prime-property adviser to wealthy buyers; F1 hospitality in Monaco, Abu Dhabi and Miami reaches its ultra-high-net-worth client base.

name: Russell Reynolds Associates
desc: Global executive search and leadership advisory firm, privately owned by its employee-shareholders, with 47 offices in 25 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1,120M in 2024 (USD 1,039M in 2023), No. 2 of Hunt Scanlon's Big Five global search firms
markets: Executive search and leadership advice for boards and companies from 47 offices across 25 countries
rationale: Board-level adviser whose clients fill F1 Paddock Club; hospitality platform with peers ManpowerGroup and Randstad already in the sport.

name: CDM Smith
desc: Employee-owned US engineering and construction firm focused on water, environment, transportation and energy infrastructure projects worldwide.
capacity_detail: Environmental services revenue USD 1,203.2M in 2023, rank 27 on ENR's 2024 Top 200 Environmental Firms; employee-owned per Wikipedia
markets: Infrastructure engineering for public and private clients in the US and abroad, with 14% of environmental revenue outside the US
rationale: Engineering firm could showcase sustainability work via F1's net-zero programme, as AtkinsReális does with its F1 partnership.

name: Sidara (Dar Al-Handasah)
desc: Privately owned engineering and design collective led by Dar, with pillars Perkins&Will, TYLin, Currie & Brown and Wood.
capacity_detail: Combined group revenue over USD 8.5bn with 55,000+ staff after completing the Wood acquisition (Mar 2026)
markets: Design and engineering across the Middle East, Africa, Asia, Europe and North America; Dar alone has 60 offices
rationale: Gulf-rooted engineering group now global after buying Wood; F1's Middle East races and AtkinsRéalis precedent suit a brand-building push.

name: Pamesa
desc: Spanish ceramic tile group from Castellón with ceramics, energy and raw-materials businesses, owned and chaired by Fernando Roig.
capacity_detail: Consolidated revenue EUR 1,147M in 2025 (EUR 1,132M in 2024) across ceramics, energy and raw materials
sponsorships: Villarreal CF (La Liga), Valencia Basket, Pamesa Teruel Voleibol; Aspar Team and padel player Daniel Sanyo Gutierrez added in 2024
markets: Ceramic tiles made in Castellón province and Teruel, sold in Spain and export markets
rationale: Established sports sponsor already backing the Aspar motorcycle racing team; F1 would extend its tile brands to architects worldwide.

name: MEWA
desc: German family-run textile service company renting and cleaning workwear, wiping cloths and mats from 54 sites in 15 countries.
capacity_detail: Naming sponsor of Mainz 05's Bundesliga stadium, Mewa Arena, since July 2021 (still the current name)
sponsorships: Mewa Arena naming, Mainz 05 (Bundesliga) since 2021; partner of easyCredit BBL and Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe cycling
markets: Textile services for industrial and trade customers from 54 sites in 15 European countries
rationale: Workwear brand for mechanics and industry; F1 garages showcase workwear, and Mewa already funds Bundesliga and pro cycling.

name: Fujitec
desc: Japanese maker of elevators, escalators and moving walkways, delisted in March 2026 after an EQT tender offer.
capacity_detail: Consolidated net sales JPY 241.25bn in the year to March 2025; EQT's Bospolder1 took 79.3% in Dec 2025, delisted Mar 2026
markets: Elevator and escalator manufacturing, installation and maintenance in Japan and international markets
rationale: Newly private under EQT, Fujitec could raise its global profile against Otis, Kone and Schindler with an engineering-led F1 tie-up.

name: MCJ
desc: Japanese holding company for Mouse Computer and other PC brands, taken private by Bain Capital in 2026.
capacity_detail: Consolidated revenue JPY 207.17bn in the year to March 2025; Bain Capital's BCPE Meta Cayman took 74.91% in Apr 2026, delisted Jun 2026
markets: Develops, manufactures and sells PCs and peripherals mainly in Japan through Mouse Computer
rationale: Gaming-PC maker could use F1's esports and sim-racing following to build brand awareness, as Lenovo and HP do.

name: Sizzling Platter
desc: US multi-brand restaurant franchisee operating about 750 Little Caesars, Wingstop, Jersey Mike's, Dunkin' and other outlets.
capacity_detail: Bain Capital agreed to buy it from CapitalSpring in a deal reported at over USD 1bn including debt (Apr 2025)
markets: About 750 restaurants across eight brands in the United States and Mexico
rationale: Franchise operator rather than brand owner; F1 relevance limited to local US race promotions near its restaurant markets.

name: Albert
desc: Los Angeles fintech offering a personal financial assistant app for budgeting, saving, banking and investing, founded by Yinon Ravid.
capacity_detail: Official jersey patch partner of the NBA's Los Angeles Lakers from July 2026; also raised USD 173M in equity to 2021
sponsorships: Los Angeles Lakers jersey patch (Jul 2026); WNBA patches with LA Sparks, Dallas Wings (2025) and Atlanta Dream (2026)
markets: US consumers using its app for budgeting, savings and banking services; says over 10 million people trust it
rationale: Heavy NBA and WNBA patch spender targeting young US consumers; F1's fast-growing US audience suits fintech peers like Cash App.

name: MKM
desc: UK builders merchant supplying timber, building materials and tools to trade customers from about 130 branches.
capacity_detail: Turnover GBP 1.02bn in 2024 (GBP 945M in 2023), sixth in UK merchant Top 20; group is a private limited company
sponsorships: Naming rights to Hull City's MKM Stadium under a five-year deal from June 2021
markets: Builders merchant branches across the UK, expanding in 2024 to Colchester, Cardiff, Shrewsbury, Workington and Rotherham
rationale: Stadium sponsor with UK-wide trade customers; British Grand Prix hospitality and a UK team tie-up could support branch growth.
